To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we propose a novel GP-B$^{\textbf{2}}$M model that can effectively model multi-label correlations, and conduct AL through an integrated model that can capture both label and feature uncertainty.

we propose a novel integrated Gaussian process-Bernoulli mixture model to accurately quantify a sample's contribution to a correlated (hence potentially large) label space and select the most informative samples to annotate, which leads to significant improvement of the multi-label classification model.

a Gaussian Process-Bayes Bernoulli M ulti-Label active learning model is developed that is capable of accurately quantifying the informativeness of a data sample for cost-effective label annotation, and that the GP-B$^3$M model achieves the state-of-the- art multi-label active learning performance in terms of the label annotation efficiency and label prediction accuracy.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions: (i) How to effectively quantify the contribution of a data sample to a correlated multi-label space?
the development of a novel GP-B$^3$M model for multi-label active learning.
developing a principled and efficient AL method that can effectively and cost-efficiently annotate multi-label data for training MLC algorithms.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
we proposed an effective multi-label active learning framework to tackle the challenges of sparse labels and correlated labels.

our GP-B$^3$M model is a novel and effective approach for multi-label active learning, which can accurately quantify a data point's contribution to a correlated and sparse label space and select the most informative samples.
the proposed model achieves state-of-the-art performance on multi-label active learning.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
our model can be used for both multi-label classification and multi-label active learning.

the proposed method can be applied in a wide variety of multi-label classification problems, and the model can be used as a tool in the active learning process to select the most informative samples to annotate, thus reducing the annotation cost.
the model is a principled way of integrating label correlations and feature information for AL in MLC.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, by jointly modeling the feature-label mapping and the label correlations, a principled AL sampling strategy can be derived for multi-label data.

the GP-B$^3$M can be used as a principled and general framework for multi-label AL, and it can be easily extended to handle other AL problems such as multi-class AL, multi-task AL, etc., by simply replacing the B$^3$ component with other appropriate models.

, in order to achieve the most informative data selection for AL, the model should be able to accurately quantify a sample's overall contribution (i.e., label correlations) to a label space and the uncertainty of its feature representation (i.e., feature uncertainty).
